newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay Pacific likely to scrap more flights.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Pacific likely to scrap more flights.

text.p: Hong Kong's flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd was likely to cancel 18 flights on Monday because of engine problems on its 11 Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircrafts an airline spokesman said.

"We had 18 cancellations on Saturday and 18 yesterday. At the moment it looks like again it's going to be about 18 flights today," Cathay Pacific spokesman Charlie Steward-Cox told the Hong Kong government radio.
"We don't have a definitive date yet. But it is probably in a week," he said.
However, Steward-Cox said it would take a much longer time to resolve the engine fault which also caused Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd to ground its A330-300 fleet.

The groundings on Saturday followed an emergency landing by a Dragonair A330-300 at Subic Bay in the Philippines on Friday after the plane developed trouble in one of its two Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines en route from Hong Kong to Kota Kinabalu in Malaysia.
It was the fifth time since November that a Cathay Pacific or Dragonair A330-300 had made a single-engine landing.
Rolls-Royce said on Friday that gearbox bearings were to blame for the problems with the Trent 700s, which were introduced in March 1995.
